item.text: {"summary":"Draft is mostly coherent but has a blocking resolver inconsistency because the registered ALFRED vintage URL appears unable to contain the June 2026 first print while the forecast rule describes a later BEA/ALFRED first-print resolver.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"blocking","summary":"The forecast simultaneously uses the ledger URL with vintage_date=2026-06-25 and a rule resolving to the June 2026 first print expected around 2026-07-31; these cannot both be the operative resolver without an explicit discrepancy note in the final fields.","actionRequested":"Keep the registered slug/dataPointId/source URL, but make the resolver text explicitly say the ledger URL/vintage is the binding target and that it appears inconsistent with the June first-print release date; do not imply a different ALFRED vintage will be used unless the ledger is corrected."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The interval claims sigma = 3.5 from a recent official-source reference-class dispersion, but the sample or calculation for that sigma is not shown beyond four recent positive monthly changes.","actionRequested":"Name the realized-volatility sample used for sigma = 3.5, or state that it is a judgmental uncertainty allowance above the recent four-month drift dispersion."},{"rubricItem":"tails","severity":"warning","summary":"Tail scenarios are directionally relevant but still generic, especially the upside administrative/retroactive-payment case and downside adjustment correction case.","actionRequested":"Tie tails more concretely to W823RC1 first-print mechanics, such as unusual lump-sum benefit processing, seasonal-adjustment revision behavior in first vintage, or beneficiary/payment-count surprise."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Make resolutionSource match the ledger source more exactly, e.g. registered ALFRED W823RC1 first-print mirror, while noting BEA Table 1 as the underlying source.","In the compact prior/update/interval step, mention that the 2026 COLA is already embedded in the May anchor before applying the +2.8 drift."]}
